alignments.note: μηκέτι → no longer, the two-word adverb taken whole.

Circumstantial participle rendered as a finite clause: the supplied subordinator when, the subject we and the modal could are rule 7 and rule 86 helpers on the participle, which carries the subordination itself; head on the lexical verb forbear under rule 17.

εὐδοκήσαμεν → we thought it good, subject and dummy object riding along under rules 7 and 9. Head on thought, the word rendering the δοκ- stem, on rule 104's treatment of εὐ- compounds (εὐάρεστος → well pleasing heads on pleasing); a head on good, taking the phrase as a light-verb rendering under rule 17, remains defensible.

καταλειφθῆναι → to be left behind; the infinitival marker and passive auxiliary are helpers under rules 7 and 9, and behind realizes the κατα- preverb inside the verb's own unit under rule 106. Head on the verb word left.
